admission.justification: Three publishing routes share one identity builder, and a subject taken from the shared master artifact would tell the developer a leaf landed when its master did — or the reverse. The per-leaf subject cases pin each route's identity against a real contract.

applicability: Terminal-notice subjects and occurrence identities for leaf enclosures, ordinary series contracts and admitted direct leaf generations.
conditions: A leaf enclosure names its own canonical leaf document and never borrows its master when unresolved; an ordinary series contract names its own master document. A direct landing names the immutable admitted leaf reference rather than its enclosing series master.
Identity carries the resolved subject key plus the native occurrence discriminator, so exact retries retain identity and distinct direct generations stay distinct.
A notice for a task the queue cannot name is not written at all.
exclusions: Attributing a leaf's landing or abandonment to its master.
Inventing a document reference for a taskless subject.
Changing a completed native publication because a notice could not be written.

evidence: notes/reports/reviewer/267804e5-dd71-51e8-8f1d-d975effaaeaf/role-launch/round4/L190-fix-verification-R4.json#L190-R1-F05; Prior sealed closure retained; not reopened in fixed-list R4.

statement: A terminal notice names the publishing task's canonical document: its own leaf for a leaf enclosure or direct leaf generation, and its own master for an ordinary series contract.
